newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's minister quits over corruption allegations.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's minister quits over corruption allegations.

text.p: Ghana's Interior Minister Emmanuel Osei-Owusu has resigned following the publication of a report into corruption allegations against him, a government statement said on Monday.
President Jerry Rawlings had accepted the resignation, which takes effect from November 1, it added.

Owusu sent in his resignation after the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice published a report on its investigations into alleged illegal enrichment by himself and three other senior public officials.
Owusu said in his resignation letter that he would go to court to challenge the commission's conclusions about him, said the official statement from the president's office.
"(Owusu) described the conclusions by the CHRAJ as grossly unfair and highly disputable in the face of facts and evidence available," the statement said.

"The alternative open to him at this point was to resign from his office, to enable him to concentrate all his time and energies on seeking justice for himself," it added, quoting from the resignation letter.
Owusu, a retired army colonel, has been interior minister since March 1992.
